questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does LAN stand for?
questions.hint: Think 'local' — like one school or one house.
questions.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network. It covers a small geographical area, like a school, office or home.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does WAN stand for?
questions.hint: It's the opposite of 'local' — much bigger.
questions.explanation: WAN stands for Wide Area Network. It covers a large geographical area — the internet is the biggest WAN in the world.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these is the best example of a WAN?
questions.hint: WANs span huge distances — across cities or countries.
questions.explanation: The Internet is the world's largest WAN, connecting millions of smaller networks across the globe.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is the main job of a router?
options: To direct data between different networks
To display images on a screen
questions.answer: To direct data between different networks
questions.hint: Think about what 'route' means — finding the way.
questions.explanation: A router forwards data packets between networks. At home, your router connects your LAN to the internet (a WAN).

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What piece of network hardware connects your home network to the Internet?
questions.hint: It has lights on the front and Wi-Fi comes from it.
questions.explanation: A router connects your home LAN to the wider internet (a WAN), routing data packets between them.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which device is used to connect multiple devices together on a single LAN?
questions.hint: Not a router — this one only deals with devices inside one network.
questions.explanation: A switch connects multiple devices on the same LAN and forwards data only to the device it is meant for.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize
Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of the following are advantages of using a network? (Select all that apply)
questions.hint: Two of these are actually disadvantages or wrong.
questions.explanation: Networks let you share files, share devices like printers, and communicate easily. Viruses can spread MORE easily on networks, and computers are dependent on the network working.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of an INPUT device?
questions.hint: Input = data going INTO the computer.
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device — it sends data into the computer. Monitors, speakers and printers are all output devices.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these are OUTPUT devices? (Select all that apply)
questions.hint: Output = data coming OUT of the computer to you.
questions.explanation: Monitors, speakers and printers all output data from the computer. Microphones, mice and webcams are input devices.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does CPU stand for?
questions.hint: It's the 'brain' of the computer — three words.
questions.explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit. It carries out instructions and is often called the 'brain' of the computer.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does RAM stand for?
questions.hint: Starts with 'Random'.
questions.explanation: RAM stands for Random Access Memory. It holds data and programs while they are being used. It's volatile — contents are lost when power is off.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does ROM stand for?
questions.hint: You can read from it, but you can't change it.
questions.explanation: ROM stands for Read Only Memory. It's non-volatile — its contents stay even with no power. It usually holds the start-up instructions for a computer.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which statement about RAM is correct?
options: RAM keeps data when the computer is switched off
RAM is slower than the hard disk
RAM loses its contents when the computer is switched off
RAM is used only for permanent storage
questions.answer: RAM loses its contents when the computer is switched off
questions.hint: Think about what 'volatile' means.
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory — it loses its contents when power is removed. It's much faster than the hard disk and is used for temporary working storage.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which type of storage has NO moving parts and is faster than a traditional hard drive?
questions.hint: 'Solid State' — nothing spins inside it.
questions.explanation: An SSD (Solid State Drive) uses flash memory and has no moving parts. It's faster, quieter and more shock-resistant than an HDD (Hard Disk Drive).

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does SSD stand for? (3 words)
questions.hint: Solid... State... ?
questions.explanation: SSD stands for Solid State Drive. It's a type of storage that uses flash memory chips instead of spinning disks.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does HDD stand for? (3 words)
questions.hint: Hard... Disk... ?
questions.explanation: HDD stands for Hard Disk Drive — a storage device that uses magnetic spinning disks (platters) to store data.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these is NON-VOLATILE (keeps its contents when the power goes off)?
questions.hint: Where do your saved files live when the computer is off?
questions.explanation: An SSD is non-volatile — your saved files stay on it when the power is off. RAM, CPU cache and registers are all volatile.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Why does a computer need both RAM and a hard drive (or SSD)?
options: RAM is cheap, so it stores everything permanently
The hard drive is fast, so it does the calculations
RAM is fast for active work; the hard drive stores files permanently
They do the same job, just in different places
questions.answer: RAM is fast for active work; the hard drive stores files permanently
questions.hint: One is fast but temporary; the other is slower but permanent.
questions.explanation: RAM is fast but volatile — used while programs are running. The hard drive/SSD is slower but non-volatile — used for keeping files when the computer is off.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which component is responsible for actually carrying out the instructions of a program?
questions.hint: The 'brain' of the computer.
questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) carries out the instructions of programs by fetching, decoding and executing them.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does NIC stand for in computer networking?
questions.hint: It's the hardware that lets a computer join a network.
questions.explanation: NIC stands for Network Interface Card. It's the hardware (built in or plug-in) that lets a computer connect to a network — wired or wireless.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize
Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of the following is needed to connect to the Internet from home?
options: A modem/router and an Internet Service Provider (ISP)
questions.answer: A modem/router and an Internet Service Provider (ISP)
questions.hint: You need a device AND a company to provide the connection.
questions.explanation: To get on the Internet from home you need a router/modem AND a contract with an Internet Service Provider (ISP) like BT, Sky or Virgin.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A small business has 15 computers in one office, all connected with cables to share a printer and files. What kind of network is this?
questions.hint: One office = small area = local.
questions.explanation: A network in a single office is a LAN (Local Area Network) because it covers a small geographical area.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of the following are typically TRUE of a WAN compared to a LAN? (Select all that apply)
options: Usually owned by a single organisation
Uses leased communication lines or public infrastructure
answer: Uses leased communication lines or public infrastructure
questions.hint: WANs are bigger but not usually owned by one company, and not always faster.
questions.explanation: WANs cover large areas, connect multiple LANs and use leased/public infrastructure. They are usually NOT owned by one organisation and are typically SLOWER than LANs because of the distances involved.

further_learning.title: Computer Networks and Data Transmission – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Bertie's laptop is slow when he opens lots of tabs but has plenty of empty hard drive space. Which upgrade is most likely to help?
questions.hint: The issue is running lots of things at once, not storing files.
questions.explanation: Lots of tabs use lots of RAM. Adding more RAM lets the computer keep more data active at once without slowing down. More hard drive space wouldn't help when storage isn't the bottleneck.

further_learning.title: Computer Systems and Data Science – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is the name for a small unit of data that is sent across a network?
questions.hint: It rhymes with 'jacket'.
questions.explanation: Data sent across a network is split into small chunks called packets. Each packet has an address so routers know where to send it.
